payload.content:
Based on your saved profile (undergraduate student):

For your saved undergraduate major, to register courses at UAEU, first ensure your academic advisor has set your Degree Works plan as Active and Locked.

Then, go to the UAEU website, sign in, navigate to MyUAEU > eServices > Student > Student Registration, check for any holds under Prepare for Registration, and select Register for Classes.

Choose your intended term, continue to Plans, select your desired courses by viewing their sections, add the section to your plan, then press Submit to finalize registration; verify that your status shows Registered or Save Successful.

If a section is full (Closed Section), you may request an override or select a different course with available seats; to drop a course, use the Action > Drop-Web option and submit the change.

payload.content:
Based on your saved profile (undergraduate student):

For your saved undergraduate status, to register courses at UAEU, first ensure your advisor has set your Degree Works plan to Active and Locked.

Then, sign in at the UAEU website, go to MyUAEU > eServices > Student > Student Registration, check for any holds under Prepare for Registration, and select Register for Classes.

Choose the intended term, continue to Plans, select your desired course, view available sections, and add the section to your registration cart.

Adding a course places it in Pending status; you must press Submit and verify that the status changes to Registered with a confirmation of Save Successful.

If sections are full or time conflicts occur, you will get errors; closed sections require an override request or choosing another available course.

To drop a course, use Action > Drop-Web and submit your request through the registration portal.

cases.expected: Give official registration steps and the appropriate registration/portal link. Do not claim to register courses or access the student’s live record.

conversation.question: How do I register my courses at UAEU?

payload.content:
Based on your saved profile (undergraduate student):

For your saved undergraduate status, to register courses at UAEU, first sign in to the UAEU website and go to MyUAEU > eServices > Student > Student Registration.

Check for any holds under 'Prepare for Registration' and then select 'Register for Classes', choose the intended term, continue, select your plan, pick the desired course, view available sections, and add the section to your registration list.

Adding a course places it in Pending status; you must press Submit to finalize registration and verify that the status shows Registered or Save Successful.

steps.title: Prepare

steps.title: Choose a section

steps.title: Complete registration

sources.title: UAEU Course Registration Service Guide
sources.evidenceText: Official registration guide pages 2–4: advisor must set the Degree Works plan Active & Locked. Open UAEU website > Sign In > MyUAEU > eServices > Student > Student Registration. Check Prepare for Registration/holds. Choose Register for Classes, intended term, Continue, Plans, desired course, View Sections, then Add the section. Add produces Pending, not enrollment; press Submit and verify Registered/Save Successful. Full sections and time conflicts cause errors. Page 5: Closed Section means no seats; a CLOSED SECTION override may be requested, otherwise choose a course with space. Dropping: Action > Drop-Web > Submit. Page 7 says choose Plan, not manual CRN entry.

cases.expected: Answer the requested public university service for this audience, cite a relevant official readable source, distinguish public guidance from live private access, and request genuinely missing applicant details.

conversation.question: How do I apply to UAEU as an international undergraduate?

payload.content:
To apply to UAEU as an international undergraduate student, you must have an accredited Grade 12 certificate and obtain UAE Ministry of Education equivalency if your high-school certificate is from outside the MOE curriculum; you must be no older than 35, have no previous academic or disciplinary dismissal from any educational institution, and be medically fit. English proficiency requirements include Grade 12 English with 90%, IELTS Academic 5.5, TOEFL ITP 525, or iBT 70. Admission is competitive, and you should use the UAEU online application route.

The UAEU online application process for bachelor's programs involves creating or signing into the linked system, submitting your application, paying AED 210 including 5% VAT, uploading a photo, passport, and Emirates ID, and then receiving email updates about your application status; the service aims to deliver a decision within 12 days but this is not a guaranteed admission deadline or decision.

cases.expected: Answer the requested public university service for this audience, cite a relevant official readable source, distinguish public guidance from live private access, and request genuinely missing applicant details.

conversation.question: What are the general graduate admission requirements?

payload.content:
To apply for a master's degree at UAEU, you generally need a related accredited bachelor's degree with a GPA of at least 3.0 out of 4.0 and an IELTS Academic score of 6.0; if your IELTS is 5.5, you may be conditionally admitted with requirements to improve your English and academic performance during your first semester.

For PhD admission, the general minimum requirements include a master's degree with a GPA of at least 3.0, a bachelor's degree GPA of at least 2.5, and an IELTS Academic score of 6.5 for English-medium study or an English dissertation, with some exemptions for native English speakers or English-medium master's graduates.

PhD applicants must submit certified degree certificates and transcripts, Ministry of Education equivalency if required, English and Arabic proficiency certificates (depending on language of study), two recommendation letters, a CV, a valid passport (plus Emirates ID for UAE residents or family book for UAE nationals), and a personal photo.

citations.title: UAEU College of Graduate Studies Admission
citations.sourceSection: Masters requirements and conditional admission; PhD requirements and Required Documents for PhD programs
citations.evidenceText:
Graduate application and requirements
- Apply through the official online link on the College of Graduate Studies admission page after choosing the degree and program. Program standards can be higher; meeting minimums does not guarantee admission.
- For a predominantly English-taught master's, the general baseline is a related accredited bachelor's degree, GPA 3.0/4.0 and IELTS Academic 6.0. IELTS 5.5 is a conditional route, not automatic eligibility: reach 6.0 by the end of the first semester, take at most 6 credit hours initially (excluding intensive English), and earn GPA 3.0 in the first 9 credit-bearing hours. Separate conditional GPA routes exist from 2.5; Arabic-taught master's programs list IELTS 4.0.
- General PhD minimums are master's GPA 3.0, bachelor's GPA 2.5, and IELTS 6.5 for English-medium study/English dissertation; Arabic-medium PhD lists IELTS 5.0. Language-test exemptions and additional college requirements may apply.
- PhD document checklist: certified bachelor's and master's degree certificates and transcripts; Ministry of Education equivalency/certificate recognition for the previous degree as required; English proficiency certificate; Arabic proficiency certificate for Arabic-medium PhD; two recommendation letters; CV; valid passport for all applicants, plus Emirates ID for UAE residents and family book for UAE nationals; and a personal photo. Passport and ID are not interchangeable alternatives.
For English-medium PhD study or an English dissertation, IELTS Academic6.5 or equivalent is required and the test score must be less than two years old at application. The page states two exception routes: a native English speaker with a master’s from an English-medium institution in a country where English is official; or an English-medium master’s graduate with evidence of IELTS Academic6.0 or equivalent at admission to that master’s. Individual colleges may impose additional or higher standards.
